pointers.sentence: In production a message leaves through an SMTP server, over a connection costly to open (`docs/topics/email.txt`); in development and tests it goes to the console, a file, a list in memory or nowhere.

Unlike the handlers of the cache and the tasks it is not built on `BaseConnectionHandler`, and keeps nothing: `MailersHandler.__getitem__` calls `MailersHandler.create_connection` every time, and `MailersHandler.settings` reads `MAILERS` at each access, so a change to the setting is seen by the next lookup (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler`).
A path that will not import becomes an `InvalidMailer` that names it (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`).

`InvalidMailer` is an `ImproperlyConfigured` whose message begins by naming the entry when it is given the alias, and `MailerDoesNotExist` is an `InvalidMailer` that is also a `KeyError`, whose message, without that beginning, is the one shown below (`django/core/mail/exceptions.py`).
To send several times over one connection, code keeps the instance, in the documentation's way in a `with` block (`docs/topics/email.txt`).

`MAILERS` has no default: `django/conf/global_settings.py` holds it only as a comment, so `MailersHandler._is_configured`, a test of whether the settings have it, is true only in a project that defines it.

`get_connection` warns that Django 2028 will have no default mailer, unless an old email setting is defined (`warn_about_default_mailers_if_needed`), and makes the backend `EMAIL_BACKEND` names without an alias, which sends the SMTP backend to `EMAIL_HOST`, `EMAIL_PORT` and the other old settings (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:get_connection`).

`get_connection` is deprecated in 6.1, with the `connection=`, `fail_silently=` and credential arguments of the sending functions, to go in Django 2028 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`, `docs/internals/deprecation.txt`).

`get_connection` is deprecated in 6.1, with the `connection=`, `fail_silently=` and credential arguments of the sending functions, to go in Django 2028 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`, `docs/internals/deprecation.txt`).

It warns through `warn_about_external_use`, which warns only when the caller is outside Django, so that one deprecated feature built on another does not warn twice (`django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).

Defining any setting of `DEPRECATED_EMAIL_SETTINGS` beside `MAILERS` is an `ImproperlyConfigured` as the settings load (`django/conf/__init__.py:_check_email_settings_conflicts`), and reading one while `MAILERS` is defined raises `AttributeError` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

Defining any setting of `DEPRECATED_EMAIL_SETTINGS` beside `MAILERS` is an `ImproperlyConfigured` as the settings load (`django/conf/__init__.py:_check_email_settings_conflicts`), and reading one while `MAILERS` is defined raises `AttributeError` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings.__getattr__`).

It receives the keyword arguments the subclass did not consume: made for an alias, it raises `InvalidMailer` naming them as unknown options; made directly, it ignores them, warning when the maker is outside Django (`django/core/mail/backends/base.py:BaseEmailBackend.__init__`).
`BaseEmailBackend.__enter__` calls `open`, and `close` if that fails; `BaseEmailBackend.__exit__` calls `close` (`django/core/mail/backends/base.py:BaseEmailBackend.__enter__`).
Its contract, in the documentation: return the number sent; open a connection if none is open and close it after, but leave open one that was open (`docs/topics/email.txt`).
Made without an alias, it reads each option it is not given from the old setting, the port from `EMAIL_PORT` whatever the security (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.__init__`).
With `"fail_silently"`, an `OSError`, which every exception of the standard library's SMTP module is, makes `open` return `None` (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.open`).

Otherwise, under the instance's re-entrant lock, it calls `open`, returns 0 if that failed in silence, sends each message with `EmailBackend._send`, and in a `finally` clause closes the connection if this call opened it (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.send_messages`).

It requires one mailbox, encodes a domain that is not ASCII with IDNA, and returns the bare address: `"office@harbour.example"` for `"Harbour Office <office@harbour.example>"` (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.prep_address`).
The console backend writes each message's text to its `"stream"`, standard output by default, with a line of 79 hyphens after it (`django/core/mail/backends/console.py:EmailBackend.send_messages`).

The file backend is a console backend whose stream is a file: it requires `"file_path"`, a directory it creates, and its `open` opens for appending a file there named for the time and the instance's `id` (`django/core/mail/backends/filebased.py:EmailBackend.open`).

Its `send_messages` builds each message, which validates its headers, and appends a deep copy to the outbox with `EmailMessage.sent_using` set to its alias, leaving the caller's message unchanged (`django/core/mail/backends/locmem.py:EmailBackend.send_messages`).
These four are for development: the deployment check mail.E001 fails when one of them is the `"default"` mailer (`django/core/checks/mail.py:check_mailers_production_backend`).
For a test run Django gives every alias the local-memory backend ([The test framework](../testing.md)) (`django/test/utils.py:setup_test_environment`).

With `using=` it sends through that alias's mailer; without, through a backend given by the deprecated argument, or else through `django.core.mail.get_connection`, which with `MAILERS` defined is the default mailer; `using=` beside a deprecated argument is a `TypeError` (`django/core/mail/message.py:EmailMessage.send`).
`send_mail` builds an `EmailMultiAlternatives`, an HTML body as its alternative where one is given, and returns what `send` returns (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mail`).

`send_mass_mail` makes one backend and sends all its messages in one call of `send_messages`, so through the SMTP backend they share a connection, where `send_mail` opens one each time (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:send_mass_mail`).
The subject is prefixed with `EMAIL_SUBJECT_PREFIX`, `"[Django] "` by default, and the sender is `SERVER_EMAIL`, not `DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL` (`django/core/mail/__init__.py:_send_server_message`).

The sendtestemail command calls `send_mail` and, with its options, `mail_managers` and `mail_admins`, each with the alias its option --using gives (`django/core/management/commands/sendtestemail.py:Command.handle`).
